title: Naturality and additivity of the canonical Tate Weil arrows
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Let $w_0:T'_0\to T_0$ be any morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with geometric base change $w:T'\to T$. At each coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ put $T_{r,T}=\Lambda_T(r)$ and let $\tau_{r,T}:G_TT_{r,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{r,T}$ be the roots-of-unity Weil arrow of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], with twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For $r\ge0$ let $t_{w,r}:Lw^*T_{r,T}\cong T_{r,T'}$ be the canonical twist comparison and $C_w:Lw^*G_T\cong G_{T'}Lw^*$. Then
$$t_{w,r}Lw^*(\tau_{r,T})=\tau_{r,T'}G_{T'}(t_{w,r})C_{w,T_{r,T}}.$$
For a coefficient functor $R$, namely finite reduction, integral-to-finite reduction, or integral extension $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$ for a finite extension $E\subseteq L$, let $t_{R,r}:RT_{r,T}\cong T'_{r,T}$ and $C_R:RG_T\cong G'_TR$ be its canonical comparisons. Then
$$t_{R,r}R(\tau_{r,T})=\tau'_{r,T}G'_T(t_{R,r})C_{R,T_{r,T}}.$$
These equations concern the canonical arrows, including their compatible roots-of-unity inverse systems; at integral level they hold on the specified strict quotient systems and at field level on their localized/common-stage images. For $r,s\ge0$ let $\alpha_{r,s,T}:T_{r,T}\otimes^LT_{s,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{r+s,T}$ be the tensor-power identification. Additivity means
$$\alpha_{r,s,T}(\tau_{r,T}\otimes^L\tau_{s,T})\mu_{g_T;T_{r,T},T_{s,T}}=\tau_{r+s,T}G_T(\alpha_{r,s,T}).$$
The mixed identity is an equation on $T'$: put $\tau^w_{s,T}=Lw^*(\tau_{s,T})C_{w,T_{s,T}}^{-1}:G_{T'}Lw^*T_{s,T}\to Lw^*T_{s,T}$ and $a_{w,r,s}=\alpha_{r,s,T'}(1\otimes^Lt_{w,s}):T_{r,T'}\otimes^LLw^*T_{s,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{r+s,T'}$. Then
$$a_{w,r,s}(\tau_{r,T'}\otimes^L\tau^w_{s,T})\mu_{g_{T'};T_{r,T'},Lw^*T_{s,T}}=\tau_{r+s,T'}G_{T'}(a_{w,r,s}).$$ The case $r=0$ is the coefficient-unit arrow. Twists have degree zero; their reassociations with even shifts $[2r],[2s]$ have sign $1$. The roots-of-unity comparisons are those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image], the twist comparisons $t_{w,r}$ those of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], and the tensor-power identifications use the comparison $\mu$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Here finite reduction means the derived coefficient functor $-\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}A_{E,n}$ for $m\ge n\ge1$; integral-to-finite reduction is $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, and integral extension uses the completed scalar functor of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. All operations are on the finite pro-etale derived categories or their derived-complete integral, rationalized and common-stage constructible categories of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

proof.text: Apply the split theorem `geometricTateCore`, which packages the six geometric, coefficient, strict-system and root-tower clauses. Its proof is the full canonical comparison argument recorded in the original ten steps of this node; the arithmetic sign clauses are separated below.

For every integer p, the exponent 2*s*p is even, and the exponent (2*r)*(2*s) is even. The characterization `Int.negOnePow_eq_one_iff` therefore gives both displayed parity identities, including r=0, s=0 and ell=2.

Publicly re-export the existing categorical law, ordinary-comparison and scalar-comparison modules. The split preserves all constructors, the original core hole, parity proof and final theorem proof. Local canonical instance priorities and opacity are retained; no new mathematical statement or hole is added.

The old mixed shorthand composes arrows from different sources (Lw*G_T versus G_{T'}Lw*); the delivered form inserts C_w and t_{w,s} and spells out α and μ. I re-typed every equation by hand. This repairs the typing without weakening anything, and it gives exactly the parent's step-1 shorthand τ_d⊗Lf*τ_e=τ_{d+e} 'under twist additivity'; the sibling strict-system node reads the integral identities on strict systems, as the item states. Steps: (1) the composition rule c^{fh}=c^h h^{-1}(c^f) holds by the adjoint calculation with the specified compositor; (2) limit/projection argument via the integral-line lemma clauses 2-3, with only g^{-1} (an equivalence) commuting with limits; (3) the ramified exponent rule matches clause 4; (4) exactness, termwise compositor and the local-freeness argument; (5)-(6) tensor-power induction and additivity (elementary); (7) the strict-system realization uses what the tower-substitution, integral-operations and scalar-extension statements actually say; (8) rational and common stage by definition; (9) the mixed identity re-derived and the signs (−1)^{bp}=1 for b=2s. Edge cases r=0, s=0, w=id, empty schemes, ℓ=2 and ramified E⊂L all hold.
